no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

response:
{
  "headline": "SPIRE-2 failed as a development programme: Pfizer stopped the trial early on Nov 1, 2016 and discontinued bococizumab because anti-drug antibodies attenuated LDL-C lowering and injection site reactions were more frequent, even though the observed HR of 0.79 (21% RRR) was better than the calculator's predicted HR of 0.838.",
  "summary": "SPIRE-2 (NCT01975389) randomized 10,621 patients (10,564 per ClinicalTrials.gov) to bococizumab or placebo and followed them for a median of 12 months. It accrued 403 primary composite events (179 treatment vs 224 control) and reported a hazard ratio of 0.79, a 21% relative risk reduction. The calculator had predicted failure, expecting an HR of 0.838 (16.2% RRR) with only 42.5% power, based on a phase 2 placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of −53.4 mg/dL (−1.381 mmol/L). The trial did not fail for lack of an efficacy signal: Pfizer's discontinuation was a non-scientific, execution-driven decision. However, early stopping left the trial underpowered (minimum detectable HR 0.756 at 80% power) and no confidence interval was reported, so the true magnitude of benefit remains uncertain.",
  "key_evidence": [
    "HR 0.79 (21% RRR) for the primary composite of nonfatal heart attack, nonfatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina requiring urgent revascularization, or cardiovascular death — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17)",
    "403 primary events (179 treatment, 224 control) in 10,621 randomized patients (10,564 per ClinicalTrials.gov), median follow-up 12 months — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01975389 SPIRE-2",
    "Calculator expected HR 0.838 with 42.5% power and minimum detectable HR 0.756 at 80% power, based on phase 2 placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of −53.4 mg/dL (−1.381 mmol/L) — calculator output; Results of bococizumab, a monoclonal antibody against proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9, from a randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study in statin-treated subjects with hypercholesterolemia",
    "Trial stopped early on Nov 1, 2016; Pfizer discontinued bococizumab citing anti-drug antibodies causing attenuated LDL-C lowering over time and injection site reactions occurring significantly more frequently with bococizumab — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17)",
    "Phase 3 LDL-C reduction reported as −55% but not placebo-adjusted, so the true on-treatment biomarker effect in the outcome trial population is uncertain — PCSK9 Inhibition with Bococizumab Yields Mixed Results (American College of Cardiology press release, ACC.17)"
  ],
  "what_would_change_this": "A full peer-reviewed publication with confidence intervals for the HR and on-treatment LDL-C data, or a new adequately powered trial, would be needed to confirm whether the observed 21% RRR reflects a real treatment effect or an estimate inflated by early stopping.",
  "readthrough_note": "Other PCSK9 inhibitor outcome trials (FOURIER, ODYSSEY OUTCOMES) demonstrated significant benefit in similar high-risk populations, indicating that bococizumab's failure appears drug-specific (immunogenicity) rather than evidence against the PCSK9–LDL-C causal pathway."
}
